subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should LaunchAgent-managed raw-stream logging fail closed when an operator sets `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=0` or unsets it via `launchctl`, even if a generated service env file, state-dir `.env`, or config env source still contains `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM=1`?
rationale: This chooses precedence for sensitive diagnostic logging across launchd inherited env, generated service env files, state-dir `.env`, and config env; automation should not silently choose that security boundary.

options.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
options.body: Treat an explicit operator false value as disabling raw-stream writes and add status/Doctor/docs proof for hidden service-env cleanup.

options.title: Document Durable Source Precedence
options.body: Keep durable service env/config values authoritative but make status/Doctor identify the active source and document how to remove it.

options.title: Require Maintainer Repro First
options.body: Hold code changes until a macOS LaunchAgent repro captures process env, generated service env, and append behavior in one trace.

recommendation.title: Fail Closed On Explicit False
recommendation.body: Treat an explicit operator false value as disabling raw-stream writes and add status/Doctor/docs proof for hidden service-env cleanup.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and review ownership on LaunchAgent service-env behavior make this the clearest available decision route.
